postgres_requirements.rationale: A real PostgreSQL probe is MANDATORY and both harness paths are legitimately UNKNOWN because no implementing node exists yet; naming a path that does not exist would be a fabricated fact. HARNESS SHAPE, frozen: a disposable cluster ONLY via pnpm db:audit:disposable — NEVER staging, NEVER production, NEVER the canonical local stack. FIXTURE: TWO-TENANT carrying REAL rows in the NON-SELECTED organization, because a probe returning zero rows for want of data proves nothing. TWO-PHASE CONSTRUCTION is forced: the dual-member subject cannot exist while user_single_active_membership does, so it may be built only in a post-S7 phase INSIDE the disposable cluster; dropping that index elsewhere is prohibited by DROP_LAST_RULE.prohibited_shortcuts. CONNECTION REUSE IS A FIRST-CLASS HARNESS REQUIREMENT, new in R2: at least one probe MUST run on a connection that previously served an organization-scoped transaction and committed, because the custom-GUC empty-string residual is a per-CONNECTION property. This was reproduced during authorship on postgres:17-alpine: on a virgin connection current_setting('app.organization_id', true) IS NULL is TRUE and denies correctly, but after a transaction-local set_config plus COMMIT on the SAME connection the value is the EMPTY STRING (is_null false, length 0), and the R1 predicate current_setting(...)::uuid then raises SQLSTATE 22P02 'invalid input syntax for type uuid' instead of denying, while nullif(current_setting(...), '')::uuid IS NULL remains TRUE. A harness that opens a fresh connection per assertion CANNOT observe this and would have certified the R1 defect. Nine probes PG-S4-1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 are frozen in the authority; PG-S4-3 is RETIRED as vacuous. STORAGE PROBES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: they belong to the separate STORAGE_SELECTED_ORG_BOUNDARY node, because the Supabase Storage API evaluates storage.objects policies on a different database connection that never runs set_config, so no GUC-based storage probe can be production-faithful. OPERATIONAL NOTE measured on this host: a docker exec round trip costs roughly 250 ms, so a probe loop of a few dozen assertions exceeds the default per-test timeout and must set an explicit one rather than be reported as a failure.

sentinels.purpose: A uniquely-valued row planted in the NON-SELECTED organization B, in a WELDED relation. It must never appear in any result set, error payload or log line produced by a transaction scoped to organization A. It makes cross-tenant leakage assertable BY IDENTITY rather than by row count, because a count cannot distinguish 'denied' from 'no such row'.

A uniquely-valued fx_rates row with organization_id IS NULL that MUST REMAIN READABLE from a scoped transaction after the weld. This is a POSITIVE canary and the ONLY construct that can detect OVER-DENIAL: negative controls prove a forbidden row is refused and are blind by construction to a required row that has also been refused.

A uniquely-valued audit_logs row with organization_id IS NULL written from an unscoped transaction, mirroring db/migrations/0067. It must remain WRITABLE after the weld. It proves the worst-timing case: the refusal audit is emitted exactly when no organization is selected.

A uniquely-valued audit_logs row carrying a NON-NULL organization_id and one of the three frozen acquisition actions, written from an unscoped transaction in which the subject's membership was created earlier in the SAME transaction. It is the positive canary for the narrow bootstrap arm: without it, a weld that silently breaks organization founding and invitation acceptance passes every cross-tenant negative. This is the sentinel R1 lacked.

A uniquely-valued row in organization B that a superadmin subject MUST still read after S4 with no organization selected. It is the positive canary for superadmin compatibility, turning the unannounced-partial-S5 failure from an invisible behavioral regression into a RED test.

One uniquely-valued row per parent-scoped relation (impact_narratives, indicators, outcomes, stakeholder_groups) belonging to a project of organization B. Four distinct sentinels, one per relation, so that isolation is proven per relation rather than by a single aggregate assertion that a partial weld would satisfy.

positive_controls.description: [S4 | MANIFEST PRECONDITION, UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION] The two known_conditions above are the ONLY entries in docs/ops/ods/KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_v1.0.0.json at this head, read directly from that file. Both are pre-existing deferred failures of the hosted-baseline gate caused by a rehearsal artifact recorded against an older baseline manifest. Their applicability to the implementing node is UNKNOWN and MUST be re-verified with pnpm ops:test-diff at that node's own base; it could not be run here because node_modules is absent. A hosted-baseline-gate failure whose signature does NOT match these two fingerprints is a NEW failure and MUST fail closed rather than be classified as known.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-1] A dual-member subject with organization A selected READS and WRITES a row of organization A in a WELDED relation; then symmetrically with organization B selected. Both directions are required, because a one-directional probe cannot distinguish a correct selected-org weld from one hard-coded to a single organization.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-6, OVER-DENIAL] SENTINEL_SHARED_FX_RATE_POSITIVE_CANARY remains READABLE from a scoped transaction after the weld, and the equivalent shared rows of proxy_sources, financial_proxies and financial_proxy_versions remain readable under their own per-relation dispositions. This is the over-denial control for the four SHARED_REFERENCE_NULL_ORG relations.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-6, TENANTLESS WRITE] SENTINEL_TENANTLESS_REFUSAL_AUDIT_ROW is successfully INSERTed into audit_logs from a transaction in which no organization was ever selected. Proves the audit_logs disposition preserves write reachability for tenantless rows without granting them blanket cross-tenant read visibility.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-4, ENUMERATOR INTEGRITY] A dual-member subject running the selectable-membership enumerator with NO organization selected still enumerates BOTH organizations after S4. This is the load-bearing control of the node: it is the only control that catches the bootstrap deadlock in which a fail-closed weld on organizations or organization_members reduces the candidate list to ZERO and locks every subject out. It MUST run unscoped, because lib/auth/database-context.ts:933 opens that context with organizationId: null in production.

[S4 | REAL-PG, SUPERADMIN COMPATIBILITY] SENTINEL_SUPERADMIN_REACH_ROW remains readable by a superadmin subject after S4 with no organization selected. Proves S4's restrictive conjunct carries its superadmin escape and did not silently execute a partial S5. Pre-S4 and post-S4 superadmin reach must be observably identical.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-7, PARENT-SCOPED TRANSITIVITY DETERMINATION] Under the ACTUAL invoking role, determine whether a restrictive weld on public.projects transitively scopes impact_narratives, indicators, outcomes and stakeholder_groups through their project_id subqueries. These four carry NO organization_id column, so an equality weld is not expressible on them. BOTH outcomes are acceptable and the control records which holds; leaving it undetermined is not. This control determines the MECHANISM only — isolation itself is proven by N-S4-8.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-5, CLOSED-WORLD CENSUS] Let U be the organization-scoped relation universe derived INDEPENDENTLY by replaying the applied chain (db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql then db/migrations/*.sql in order), cross-checked against the pgTable declarations in db/schema.ts. Let C be the union of the S4 class arrays. Assert U == C as sets and that every name occurs in C exactly once. RED on any name in U minus C (unclassified) and on any name in C minus U (phantom). The measured figures at this head — 42 organization-scoped relations, 34 welded — are recorded as EVIDENCE and are explicitly NOT the correctness criterion: a later authorized relation may lawfully extend U and must receive an explicit disposition. U MUST NEVER be read from the S4 package under test, or the control is vacuous.

[S4 | STATIC, GUC CARRIER] db/identity-context.ts still sets app.organization_id via set_config with the third argument true (transaction-local) and still only when identity.organizationId is non-null. Both halves are load-bearing: session scope would leak tenant scope across pooled connections, and setting it unconditionally would silently change every unscoped entry point. Also asserts this remains the ONLY site in the repository that sets the GUC.

[S4 | STATIC, ACL COMPATIBILITY] S4 introduces NO new SQL function called from a policy expression. The canonical expression uses only the built-ins current_setting and nullif, which require no EXECUTE grant, and reuses only the three already-granted helpers current_user_org_ids(), current_user_is_super_admin() and current_user_role_in_org(uuid). This is the evidence that makes an ACL compatibility proof valid instead of requiring an ACL successor: evaluating a policy requires the invoking role to hold EXECUTE on every function the expression calls, so a new callable would break the ACL authority's posture of exactly three granted signatures.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-11, BOOTSTRAP AUDIT POSITIVE] With NO organization selected, a subject whose active membership in ORG_A was created earlier in the SAME transaction successfully INSERTs SENTINEL_BOOTSTRAP_ACQUISITION_AUDIT_ROW into audit_logs, carrying organization_id = ORG_A, actor_user_id = auth.uid(), and one of the three frozen acquisition actions. Reproduces the measured orderings of organization founding (app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/actions.ts:120-180, where organizations and organization_members are inserted then two audit rows are written, all in one unscoped context) and invitation acceptance (lib/invitations/service.ts:193-225 under app/invite/accept/page.tsx:53). Without this positive, a weld that silently breaks both acquisition paths passes every cross-tenant negative in this manifest.

[S4 | STATIC, UNSCOPED CALLER DISPOSITION COMPLETENESS] Enumerate from source every non-test construction of withDatabaseIdentityContext that passes organizationId: null, and assert the resulting set is EQUAL to the set of dispositioned callers in the authority's UNSCOPED_CALLER_CLOSED_WORLD. Equality in BOTH directions: RED on an undispositioned new caller, and RED on a disposition entry naming a caller that no longer exists. The count measured at this head is recorded as evidence and is NOT the assertion — a control pinned to a number is satisfied by any set of that size and says nothing about whether a new caller is safe.

negative_controls.description: [S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-1, CROSS-TENANT READ] A dual-member subject with organization A selected is DENIED SENTINEL_ORG_B_TENANT_ROW. Asserted by sentinel identity, never by row count, because a count cannot distinguish 'denied' from 'no such row'. Symmetric assertion with B selected is required.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-1, CROSS-TENANT WRITE] A dual-member subject with organization A selected is REFUSED an INSERT and an UPDATE targeting organization B in a WELDED relation. Read denial alone is insufficient: a WITH CHECK omission would leave writes open while every read control stays green.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-2, UNSELECTED READ] With no organization selected, a WELDED relation yields ZERO tenant rows. Scoped deliberately to the welded set: asserting this over the identity substrate would encode the bootstrap deadlock as a requirement rather than catching it.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-2, UNSELECTED WRITE] With no organization selected, a tenant write to a WELDED relation is REFUSED. A live 42501 does not by itself attribute the refusal to the intended layer: an RLS WITH CHECK violation is also 42501 and is evaluated BEFORE NOT NULL and foreign-key constraints, so the control must attribute the denial to the intended policy rather than infer it from the error code.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-8, REUSED CONNECTION EMPTY GUC] On a connection that previously served an organization-scoped transaction and COMMITTED, a subsequent unscoped transaction yields ZERO tenant rows and NO writes, and MUST NOT raise SQLSTATE 22P02. Reproduced during authorship on postgres:17-alpine: after a transaction-local set_config plus COMMIT, current_setting('app.organization_id', true) on that same connection is the EMPTY STRING rather than NULL, so R1's bare cast raised 22P02 instead of denying. An exception is a 500, not a refusal — and inside the governed helpers it would be swallowed by EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS into a silent false. This control is invisible to any harness that opens a fresh connection per assertion, which is exactly how the defect reached precertification.

[S4 | REAL-PG, SET-CONFIG ECHO HAZARD] A negative RLS assertion must not be satisfied by the echo row that SELECT set_config(...) itself returns. A probe that scopes and asserts in one statement can read the set_config return value as data and report an empty result set as containing the organization, or a non-empty one as empty. Scoping and assertion MUST be separate statements.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-10, MEMBERSHIP NON-VACUITY] A subject whose selection is set to ORG_A but who is NOT a member of ORG_A reads nothing and writes nothing on a WELDED relation. This is the ONLY control with the power to detect removal of the membership conjunct: every other fixture in this manifest satisfies and violates membership and selection together, so deleting membership changes no observable outcome. The state is produced by setting the GUC directly in the harness rather than through the context constructor, because db/identity-context.ts:217 refuses a non-member organization at the application layer — and the weld must hold independently of that guard, since its purpose is to be the boundary that survives an application-layer mistake.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-9, PARENT-SCOPED CROSS-ORG ISOLATION, PER RELATION] For EACH of impact_narratives, indicators, outcomes and stakeholder_groups, the corresponding SENTINEL_PARENT_SCOPED_ORG_B_ROWS row is DENIED to a dual-member subject scoped to organization A, and symmetrically. FOUR distinct assertions, not one aggregate: a partial weld that isolates only one relation would satisfy an aggregate assertion while leaving three relations open. Distinct from P-S4-7, which determines the mechanism; this control proves the outcome.

[S4 | STATIC, SCOPE DISCIPLINE, STORAGE HANDOFF] The S4 implementation diff touches NO storage surface: it does not create, drop or alter any policy on storage.objects, does not modify can_write_evidence_object or can_read_evidence_object, and does not alter their signatures or grants. By owner decision the storage selected-organization boundary is a SEPARATE required node, because the Supabase Storage API evaluates storage.objects policies on a different database connection that never runs set_config, so no GUC-based storage weld can be production-faithful. This control exists so the handoff is PROVEN rather than assumed, and so an implementer cannot quietly reintroduce the unimplementable R1 requirement.

[S4 | STATIC/REAL-PG, S5 SCOPE DISCIPLINE] S4 does NOT remove, narrow or rewrite any of the 131 effective policies carrying current_user_is_super_admin, and does NOT remove the superadmin exemption at db/identity-context.ts:217. An S4 diff touching either has executed an unannounced partial S5 outside its grant.

[S4 | REAL-PG, PG-S4-12, BOOTSTRAP AUDIT WIDENING — FIVE ARMS, EACH MUST DENY] (a) the same bootstrap audit INSERT attempted while an organization IS selected; (b) an action OUTSIDE the frozen vocabulary ('organization.created', 'membership.created', 'invitation.accepted') with no organization selected; (c) an organization the subject is NOT a member of; (d) actor_user_id different from auth.uid(); (e) any SELECT of another tenant's audit rows through the arm. Each arm corresponds to exactly one premise of the narrow bootstrap arm, and omitting any one converts it into the generic 'no selection implies membership-only access everywhere' escape that the disposition exists to prevent. Arm (a) is the most important: it is what confines the arm to genuine acquisition.

[S4 | REAL-PG, AUDIT READ SCOPING] Tenant-owned audit_logs rows of organization B are NOT readable from a transaction scoped to organization A, and are NOT readable from an unscoped transaction. Distinguishes the audit_logs disposition from the shared-reference disposition: audit_logs NULL means 'no owner', never 'every owner', and the bootstrap arm grants INSERT only — a subject must not be able to use acquisition to read another tenant's audit history.

mutation_controls.description: [S4 | MUTATION] Change the selected-organization policy from AS RESTRICTIVE to PERMISSIVE. MUST go RED. PostgreSQL combines permissive policies with OR, so a permissive selected-org term is satisfied whenever the existing membership policy is — it would enforce nothing while every positive control stayed green.

[S4 | MUTATION] Remove the membership conjunct, leaving selected-organization equality alone. MUST go RED via N-S4-7. R1 declared this mutation but carried no control able to detect it, because no R1 fixture varied membership and selection independently.
[S4 | MUTATION] Remove the selected-organization conjunct, leaving membership alone. MUST go RED. This is precisely the pre-S4 state; if the suite stays green, S4 proved nothing.
[S4 | MUTATION] Make an absent selection PERMIT access on a welded relation, for example by adding an unconditional IS NULL escape to the selected-org term. MUST go RED via N-S4-3 and N-S4-4.

[S4 | MUTATION] Add public.organizations or public.organization_members to the welded set. MUST go RED via the enumerator-integrity control P-S4-4, NOT merely via a census count. A census-only failure would misreport a total product lockout as a bookkeeping discrepancy.
[S4 | MUTATION] Reclassify public.audit_logs as a shared-reference relation, applying the generic IS NULL OR equality disjunct to it. MUST go RED via N-S4-12.
[S4 | MUTATION] Remove one relation from the closed-world census enumeration. MUST go RED via P-S4-8. Proves the census notices a DELETION.

[S4 | MUTATION] Add a new organization_id-carrying fixture relation to U without classifying it. MUST go RED via P-S4-8. Deliberately separate from M-S4-7: one proves the census notices a removal, the other an ADDITION. A census that compares its own list against itself passes both while measuring nothing.

[S4 | MUTATION] Drop the superadmin escape from S4's restrictive conjunct. MUST go RED via P-S4-6. This is the most likely S4 defect and the hardest to see in review: it revokes superadmin reach on every welded relation while producing NO diff on any superadmin-related line, because a restrictive policy ANDs against permissive disjuncts it never names.

[S4 | MUTATION] Flip the third argument of set_config('app.organization_id', <id>, true) to false, making the GUC session-scoped. MUST go RED via P-S4-9. Transaction-locality is what stops tenant scope leaking across pooled connections.

[S4 | MUTATION, CLOSURE] Add a new unscoped withDatabaseIdentityContext construction passing organizationId: null WITHOUT adding a disposition entry. MUST go RED via P-S4-12. Also mutate in the opposite direction: remove a real caller while leaving its disposition entry, which must also go RED. Proving equality in only one direction leaves the other half of the invariant untested.

[S4 | MUTATION] Remove the nullif wrapper from the canonical expression, restoring R1's bare current_setting(...)::uuid cast. MUST go RED via N-S4-5. On a reused pooled connection the bare cast raises SQLSTATE 22P02 instead of denying. A fresh-connection-only harness stays GREEN under this mutation, which is exactly how the defect survived R1 and reached precertification — so this mutation also validates that the harness genuinely reuses a connection.

[S4 | MUTATION] Add a fourth action literal to the bootstrap arm's frozen vocabulary. MUST go RED via N-S4-11(b). The vocabulary is the arm's narrowness; widening it silently is the cheapest way to turn a bootstrap exemption into a general one.

[S4 | MUTATION] Drop the unselected premise from the bootstrap arm, making it reachable while an organization IS selected. MUST go RED via N-S4-11(a). This single deletion converts the narrow arm into the generic 'no selection implies membership-only everywhere' escape, and it is the highest-severity bootstrap mutation because the arm would still look narrow — it would still name three actions and require membership.
[S4 | MUTATION] Drop the membership premise from the bootstrap arm, so any subject may write an acquisition audit row for any organization while unscoped. MUST go RED via N-S4-11(c).

[S4 | MUTATION] Weld only one of the four parent-scoped relations, leaving the other three unisolated. MUST go RED via N-S4-8. An aggregate cross-org assertion would pass this mutation; only per-relation negatives catch it.

[S4 | MUTATION, HANDOFF INTEGRITY] Reintroduce a storage weld requiring app.organization_id inside can_write_evidence_object or can_read_evidence_object. MUST go RED via N-S4-9. This is the R1 blocking defect: the requirement is unimplementable because the Storage API evaluates on a different connection, and implementing it fail-closed would deny every upload, download and delete in the product. The control exists so the defect cannot silently return under a later edit.
